summary: Frontend-only test pass of the new BOM Stock Panel on Production Confirmation > Create Production Order (synthetic Entra session seeded then deleted). ALL 8 new-feature behaviours PASS: (1) 'Check Stock' (toggle-bom-stock-panel-button) is disabled with an empty Product ID and enabled after typing; (2) opening the panel splits the card exactly in half (card 936px -> form column 443px + panel 443px, panel_x=492) and fires exactly ONE cache-only request (`live=false`) with the resolved production_model_uuid; header 'BOM Stock (x500 EA)', 'Source: Cached snapshot · as of 24/8/2026, 10:07:17 am', 2 real components with per-location breakdown; (3) reactive recompute verified - editing Quantity 500->50->200000 updated header and every Required qty / Short-by instantly with ZERO new /bom-stock-status requests (request listener counted 0); shortage styling verified at qty 200000: 'Short by 36,656.32 KG' rgb(180,35,24) font-weight 700, sufficient rows green rgb(2,122,72); (4) 'Check Live Stock' hit `live=true`, SAP was reachable and the source line switched to 'Live SAP · as of ...' with no error toast and no crash; (5) toggle closes the panel and the label flips Check Stock/Hide Stock, re-open does NOT re-fetch (0 new requests, 2 components still rendered); (6) editing Product ID resets bomStockStatus (components/source disappear); (7) switching Source of Supply on a 2-model material (MAZ42117272 _1 P2 vs _2 P3) resets the panel and the re-fetch is correctly scoped to the new production_model_uuid - model _1 returned 16 components, model _2 returned 22 different components (real per-model BOMs); (8) no-cached-BOM product (MAT) shows the graceful bom-stock-status-unavailable message 'No cached BOM found locally for this product - cannot check component stock status.' with no crash. Regression: SFG-shortage-blocks-order-creation still works end-to-end (MAZ42117272 model _2 / P3 / qty 100 -> submit -> toast 'Order request submitted', Active Orders row goes to 'SFG Shortage - Blocked' with 'Blocked before anything was created in SAP - 5 sub-assembly component(s) short at P3' and the 5-row shortage table + 'Refresh Live SFG Stock & Retry'; form reset and BOM panel closed correctly). FOUND ONE CRITICAL PRE-EXISTING BUG: the 'Refresh Live SFG Stock' button is completely non-functional (throws an uncaught TypeError, no API call at all). NOTE: a successful (non-blocked) real production order was deliberately NOT submitted - the tenant is live SAP PRD and an order cannot be undone; the shortage-blocked path exercised the whole submit/poll/Active-Orders pipeline without any SAP write.

ui_bugs.component: CreateOrderTab - Refresh Live SFG Stock button
ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: clicking it throws an uncaught runtime error `(siteOverride || siteId).trim is not a function` (pageerror confirmed twice, dev overlay shown) and NO /production-confirmation/refresh-live-sfg-stock call is ever made - the feature is dead. Root cause: line ~1190 `onClick={refreshLiveSfgStock}` passes the React click Event as the `siteOverride` argument. Fix: `onClick={() => refreshLiveSfgStock()}`. (Pre-existing, introduced in commit 74ab1de, not by the BOM-panel layout change - but it is one of the two regression items requested.) The in-row variant at line ~1428 `onClick={() => refreshLiveSfgStock(j.failure.site_id)}` is correct.

After editing Product ID or switching Source of Supply while the panel is OPEN, bomStockStatus is nulled but showBomPanel stays true, leaving a completely blank bordered box (no rows, no source line, no message, no loading text) until the user manually toggles the panel closed and open again. Suggest either auto-refetching for the new product/model or rendering a 'Click Check Live Stock to load stock for this product' placeholder.

design_issues.screen: Create Production Order - BOM Stock panel
issues: Header shows the FINISHED-GOOD unit (e.g. 'BOM Stock (x200000 EA)') while every row is in the component's own unit (KG) - correct but easy to misread; a tiny 'per order qty' label would help.

The Available/Required pair is rendered as a bare '4,852.45 / 2,000 KG' with no column header, so which number is which is only inferable; a one-line 'Available / Required' caption row would remove the ambiguity.

Cosmetic data inconsistency: for the same components the BOM panel says 'No stock found anywhere.' while the SFG-shortage block table shows 'Available in P3-SFG: unknown' - two different phrasings for zero/unknown stock on the same screen.

action_items: CRITICAL: fix `onClick={refreshLiveSfgStock}` -> `onClick={() => refreshLiveSfgStock()}` on refresh-live-sfg-stock-button (ProductionConfirmationPage.js ~line 1190). Currently the button crashes with a TypeError and never calls the API.
MEDIUM: don't leave the BOM panel visually blank after a Product ID edit / Source-of-Supply switch - auto-refetch or show a placeholder/prompt.
LOW: label the Available/Required numbers in the panel rows and align the 'no stock' vs 'unknown' wording with the SFG shortage table.
critical_code_review_comments: ProductionConfirmationPage.js is 1855 lines - far above the 700-line guideline; CreateOrderTab alone (form + BOM panel + Active Orders + shortage tables) should be split into its own module/components.

fetchBomStock's catch swallows everything into a toast - a non-2xx from the route is indistinguishable from a network error, and the panel is left blank (see the blank-panel issue). Consider keeping an inline error state inside the panel instead of only a toast.

The event-as-argument pattern that broke refreshLiveSfgStock exists because the function takes an optional positional arg; audit other `onClick={fnWithOptionalArg}` handlers in this file for the same class of bug.

rca_of_the_issue: Refresh Live SFG Stock: `refreshLiveSfgStock(siteOverride)` is wired directly as the onClick handler, so React passes the SyntheticEvent as siteOverride; `(siteOverride || siteId).trim()` then throws TypeError before the POST is issued. The handler's try/catch never runs (the throw is in the pre-flight validation), so no toast is shown and the user sees nothing happen (dev build shows the red overlay). One-line fix: wrap in an arrow function.
